entries.odia: କେତେ ଅନଉଛୁ ମତେ, ତୋଠଉଁ ସୁନ୍ଦର ମୋର ବିନୋଦିଆ, ଚାକର ରଖିବ ତତେ
entries.title: A boast that puts the onlooker in place
entries.literal_meaning: Why keep looking at me? My charming one is more beautiful than you and could keep you as a servant.
entries.explanation: The line answers someone who keeps looking at the speaker by praising another person as more beautiful. The dictionary explains “keep as a servant” here as figurative superiority in wealth or qualities, so the comparison is not a report of employment. One possible performance is a proud rebuff to an admirer: the speaker boasts that a favoured person would far outshine this supposed rival. Neither admiration nor a romantic relationship is fixed by the source gloss, however. The repeated address gives the comparison a personal, theatrical edge. Its status hierarchy is part of the rhetoric, not a measure of anyone’s human worth.
entries.meaning_odia: କେହି ଚାହିଁରହିଥିବା ବେଳେ ଏହି କଥାର ବକ୍ତା ନିଜ ପ୍ରିୟଜଣଙ୍କ ସୁନ୍ଦରତାକୁ ବଢ଼ାଇ କହି ସେହି ଚାହାଣିର ଜବାବ ଦିଅନ୍ତି। ଚାକର ରଖିବାକୁ ଅଭିଧାନ ଏଠାରେ ଧନ ବା ଗୁଣରେ ଉତ୍କୃଷ୍ଟ ହେବାର ଲକ୍ଷଣାର୍ଥ ଦେଇଛି। ଯିଏ ନିଜକୁ ପ୍ରତିଦ୍ୱନ୍ଦ୍ୱୀ ଭାବୁଥାଇପାରେ, ତାକୁ ପ୍ରିୟଜଣଙ୍କଠାରୁ ବହୁତ ତଳେ ରଖିଦେବାରେ ଏହି ଉତ୍ତରର ଖୋଚା। ଏହା ନିଜ ପ୍ରିୟଜଣଙ୍କୁ ନେଇ ଗର୍ବ ସାଙ୍ଗରେ ମିଶିଥିବା ଏକ ନାଟକୀୟ ଜବାବ ଭଳି ଶୁଣାଯାଏ; ପ୍ରେମର ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ଏହାର ଗୋଟିଏ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ପାଠ। କାମ ବା ସାମାଜିକ ସ୍ଥିତି ଦେଇ ମଣିଷର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ମାପିବାକୁ ଏହି ପାଠ ସମର୍ଥନ କରେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: A pointed comparison answers an onlooker with a boast about someone else’s beauty.
entries.odia_summary: ନିଜ ପ୍ରିୟଜଣଙ୍କ ଗର୍ବ କରି ଚାହିଁରହିଥିବା ଜଣକୁ ଖୋଚା ଦେଉଥିବା ଉତ୍ତର।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: During a light-hearted drama rehearsal, one character keeps posing to catch another character’s eye. The other quotes this line, praising someone supposedly more beautiful. The performers choose to play it as a proud rebuff to an admirer; that relationship is invented for this scene, not established by the dictionary. They treat the employment comparison as exaggeration rather than a reason to mock an occupation.
entries.cultural_context: The source supplies a figurative status comparison, not a named romance or biographical episode. Charming one renders ବିନୋଦିଆ without fixing a romantic relationship; the speaker’s gender and any historical characters are not established. The employment hierarchy should remain visible as rhetoric without being endorsed.

entries.odia: ହାଣ୍ଡିରେ ଖାଏ, ଗୋଡ଼ରେ ପଡ଼ିଲେ ଗାଧୋଇ ଯାଏ
entries.title: Good enough to eat, too much to touch
entries.literal_meaning: One eats from the pot, but goes to bathe when its contents fall on the foot.
entries.explanation: The same food is welcome in the mouth and suddenly objectionable on the foot. That abrupt change is the comic hinge of the line: acceptance in one situation turns into an elaborate response in another. The dictionary supplies the bathing sense but no separate moral gloss. Our reading treats the contrast as a possible tease about selective fastidiousness or inconsistent standards. It does not establish that bathing is always excessive, or that a particular ritual or community is being described.
entries.meaning_odia: ହାଣ୍ଡିରୁ ଖାଇବା ବେଳେ ଯାହା ଗ୍ରହଣୀୟ, ସେହି ଖାଦ୍ୟ ଗୋଡ଼ରେ ପଡ଼ିଲେ ଗାଧୋଇବାକୁ ଯିବାର କଥା ଆସୁଛି। ଏକେ ଜିନିଷକୁ ଦୁଇ ପରିସ୍ଥିତିରେ ଏତେ ଅଲଗା ଭାବେ ନେବାରେ ଏହାର ହାସ୍ୟ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଗାଧୋଇବା କ୍ରିୟାର ଉଦାହରଣ ଭାବେ କଥାଟି ଅଛି; ଅଲଗା ନୀତିକଥା ଦିଆଯାଇନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଏହି ବିପରୀତ ଆଚରଣକୁ ଧରି ଅତି ବାଛବିଚାର ବା ବଦଳୁଥିବା ମାପକାଠିକୁ ଥଟ୍ଟା କରିହୁଏ। ସ୍ୱରଟି ଘନିଷ୍ଠ ହସର ହୋଇପାରେ, ପୁଣି ତାଚ୍ଛଲ୍ୟର ମଧ୍ୟ ହୋଇପାରେ।
entries.english_summary: The contrast invites a teasing question about standards that change with the situation.
entries.odia_summary: ଏକେ ଜିନିଷ ପାଇଁ ଦୁଇ ମାପକାଠି ରଖିବାକୁ ଖୋଚା ଦେଉଥିବା ଚିତ୍ର।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A friend happily eats a sticky sweet with their fingers, then protests loudly when a little syrup touches their shoe. Another friend quotes the saying with a smile while offering a cloth. This harmless transfer is editorial, not a documented historical use.
entries.cultural_context: No named caste, purity rule or bathing custom is inferred. The interpretation of inconsistent standards is editorial close reading; the source attests the words and literal verb.

entries.odia: ଯେ ତବତ ଖାଇଛି ସେ ପଖାଳ ଖାଉ, ଯେ କିଛି ନ ଖାଇଛି ସେ ଗାଧୋଇ ଯାଉ
entries.title: More for the fed, nothing for the hungry
entries.literal_meaning: Let the one who has eaten hot rice have pakhala; let the one who has eaten nothing go off to bathe.
entries.explanation: The people already fed receive another dish, while those who have had nothing are sent away. The dictionary’s figurative sense of going to bathe—being deprived of an enjoyment—makes the exclusion explicit. The pairing sounds almost like an orderly instruction, but the distribution it describes is upside down. It can give a speaker a pointed way to expose favouritism: those already served are served again, and unmet need is dismissed. This is an editorial reading of the contrast, not a rule about who deserves food.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯିଏ ଗରମ ଭାତ ଖାଇସାରିଛି, ତାକୁ ପୁଣି ପଖାଳ; ଯିଏ କିଛି ଖାଇନାହିଁ, ତାକୁ ଗାଧୋଇ ଯିବାକୁ କୁହାଯାଉଛି। ଗାଧୋଇ ଯିବାର ଲକ୍ଷଣାର୍ଥ ଅଭିଧାନରେ କୌଣସି ଲାଭ ବା ଉପଭୋଗରୁ ବଞ୍ଚିତ ହେବା। ଶୁଣିବାକୁ ବଣ୍ଟନର ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦେଶ ଭଳି, ହେଲେ ଭାଗବଣ୍ଟାଟି ପୂରା ଓଲଟା। ଯାହାର ମିଳିସାରିଛି ତାକୁ ଆହୁରି ମିଳୁଛି, ଯାହାର କିଛି ନାହିଁ ତାକୁ ଦୂରେଇ ଦିଆଯାଉଛି—ଏହି ଅନ୍ୟାୟକୁ ଦେଖାଇବାରେ କଥାଟିର କଟାକ୍ଷ ଲାଗିପାରେ। ଏଠାରେ ଆମେ ସେହି ବୈଷମ୍ୟକୁ ଚିହ୍ନଟ କରି ପଢ଼ୁଛୁ, ତାକୁ ଠିକ୍ ବୋଲି କହୁନାହୁଁ।
entries.english_summary: A seemingly orderly instruction exposes an unfair distribution: more for those already served.
entries.odia_summary: ଯାହାର ମିଳିସାରିଛି ତାକୁ ଆହୁରି, ବାକି ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ କିଛି ନାହିଁ—ଏହି ଓଲଟା ବଣ୍ଟନର କଟାକ୍ଷ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A workshop gives extra notebooks to participants who already received supplies, while late arrivals are told there are none for them. One participant quotes the saying to question the arrangement and asks for the remaining notebooks to be shared fairly.
entries.cultural_context: The hot-rice sense of ତବତ is independently checked in a second entry of the same dictionary lineage (revision221175), not an independent witness to the saying. Pakhala is retained as the food name. Unlike existing166, this is about unequal allocation and exclusion, not deciding between dishes before asking.

entries.odia: ରଣ, ବଣ, ଛଣ, ବାଙ୍କିରଜା ଥାଇ ବୋଇଲେ ମୋ ଢୁଢୁଆ ବାଇଗଣ
entries.title: The king’s answer is a brinjal
entries.literal_meaning: Rana, forest and thatching grass—the king of Banki answers with “my dhudhua brinjal.”
entries.explanation: The opening piles up three resources with a quick rhyme; the reply sets one unassuming vegetable against them. The dictionary explains the joke through a comparison of revenues: it says Dampara’s river fish, forest products and thatching grass brought less than Banki’s tax on the silted land where these brinjals grew. That explanation gives the king’s answer its boastful force: what looks like a modest crop may be the more valuable resource. This is the dictionary’s account, not a revenue comparison independently established here. Its conversational appeal lies in the surprise of the small-looking answer to a grand list.
entries.meaning_odia: ରଣ, ବଣ, ଛଣ—ତିନୋଟି ସମ୍ପଦର ନାଁ ମିଳାଇ କହିବା ପରେ ଉତ୍ତରରେ ଆସୁଛି ମାତ୍ର ବାଇଗଣ। ଅଭିଧାନର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଅନୁସାରେ ଡାମ୍ପଡ଼ାର ନଦୀମାଛ, ଜଙ୍ଗଲଜାତ ଦ୍ରବ୍ୟ ଓ ଛଣର ଆୟଠାରୁ ବାଙ୍କିର ବାଇଗଣ ଫଳୁଥିବା ପଟୁଜମିର ଖଜଣା ଅଧିକ ଥିଲା। ଏହି ଉତ୍ସକଥା ଧରି ପଢ଼ିଲେ, ସାଧାରଣ ଦେଖାଯାଉଥିବା ଫସଲକୁ ନେଇ ଉତ୍ତରରେ ଗର୍ବ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ବଡ଼ ତାଲିକାକୁ ଛୋଟ ଦେଖାଯାଉଥିବା ଗୋଟିଏ ଜିନିଷ ଟପିଯିବାରେ କଥାଟିର ଚମକ। ସେହି ରାଜସ୍ୱ ତୁଳନାକୁ ଆମେ ଏଠାରେ ସ୍ୱତନ୍ତ୍ର ଐତିହାସିକ ତଥ୍ୟ ଭାବେ ଯାଞ୍ଚ କରିନାହୁଁ।
entries.english_summary: A modest-looking crop supplies the surprising answer to a grand list of resources.
entries.odia_summary: ବଡ଼ ସମ୍ପଦତାଲିକାକୁ ସାଧାରଣ ବାଇଗଣର ଚମକପ୍ରଦ ଉତ୍ତର।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: At a school fundraiser, one group lists its elaborate stalls. Another points out that the plain seedling stall earned the most. A teacher quotes the brinjal line and explains the dictionary’s comparison, using it to tease the assumption that the grandest display must bring the best result.
entries.cultural_context: Banki and Dampara belong to the source’s regional explanation. No reign, date, actual royal conversation, verified revenue figure or origin event is claimed. The modern fundraising application is editorial; the dictionary’s botanical description is not a current taxonomic certification.

entries.odia: ବୁଢ଼ା ବଳଦକୁ ଜୂଆଁଣିଆ ଘାସ ଖାଉ କି ନ ଖାଉ ମେଲି ଦେଇ ଆସ
entries.title: Leaving care at the gate
entries.literal_meaning: Give the old bull coarse juannia grass; whether it eats or not, let it loose and come away.
entries.explanation: The food is offered, but whether the old animal can use it is treated as no concern of the giver. The dismissive ending is the revealing part: doing something that resembles care becomes an excuse to stop caring about the outcome. The source defines the grass as coarse and tough; it does not give a separate figurative gloss. Our reading hears a picture of perfunctory attention, especially when someone’s needs have changed. Quoting it critically can draw attention to neglect rather than recommend the conduct it describes.
entries.meaning_odia: ବୁଢ଼ା ବଳଦକୁ ମୋଟା କରଡ଼ା ଘାସ ଦେଇଦେଲେ, ହେଲେ ସେ ଖାଇପାରିଲା କି ନାହିଁ ସେଥିରେ ଆଉ ଧ୍ୟାନ ନାହିଁ। ମେଲି ଦେଇ ଚାଲିଆସିବାର ଶେଷକଥାରେ ଏହି ଅବହେଳା ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ହୁଏ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଘାସକୁ ମୋଟା ଓ କରଡ଼ା ବୋଲି କହିଛି; ଅଲଗା ଲକ୍ଷଣାର୍ଥ ଦେଇନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଏହା କେବଳ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ସାରିଦେବା ଭଳି ଯତ୍ନର ଚିତ୍ର—ଯାହା ପାଇଁ ଦିଆଗଲା, ତାହାର କାମରେ ଲାଗିଲା କି ନାହିଁ ଦେଖାଗଲା ନାହିଁ। ଏହି ଅବହେଳାକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରି କଥାଟି ବ୍ୟବହାର କରିହୁଏ, ତାହାର ଅନୁକରଣ କରିବା ପାଇଁ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: An offer of care means little when no one checks whether it meets the recipient’s needs.
entries.odia_summary: ଯତ୍ନ ନାଁରେ କିଛି ଦେଇଦେବା ଓ ତାହା କାମରେ ଲାଗୁଛି କି ନାହିଁ ଦେଖିବା ଏକ କଥା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A club sends a complicated online form to a member who has already said they cannot use that system. When someone says “We sent it, so our job is done,” another member quotes the saying to challenge that indifference and offers to help complete the form.
entries.cultural_context: The analogy is read critically, not as animal-care advice or an assertion that older people have less value. The source spelling ଜୂଆଁଣିଆ in the quoted line is retained although the headword has ଜୁଆଁଣିଆ. No species or agricultural history is inferred.
